Linear polarization–direction correlations in γ-ray scattering
experiments
Christian Iliadis1,2 and Udo Friman-Gayer1,2
1 Department of Physics & Astronomy, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, NC 27599-3255, USA
2 Triangle Universities Nuclear Laboratory (TUNL), Duke University, Durham, North Carolina 27708, USA
Received: date / Revised version: date
Abstract. Scattering measurements with incident linearly polarized γ rays provide information on spins,
parities, and γ-ray multipolarity mixing coeﬃcients, and, therefore, on the nuclear matrix elements involved
in the transitions. We present the general formalism for analyzing the observed angular correlations. The
expressions are used to compute three-dimensional radiation patterns, which are important tools for op-
timizing experimental setups. Frequently, γ-ray transitions can proceed via two multipolarities that mix
coherently. In such cases, the relative phases of the nuclear matrix elements are important when comparing
results from diﬀerent measurements. We discuss diﬀerent phase conventions that have been used in the
literature and present their relationships. Finall
